authority: Operator-directed ticket (plans/tickets_phase8_review.md ticket 6, ST-1). Application of already-ratified rules (the gate-result input-fingerprint contract; §9.4 durable-decision rule). NOT a constitutional amendment.
ticket: ST-1 (plans/tickets_phase8_review.md ticket 6). 'Phase 3-6 staleness: content, not mtime' — carried from HANDOFF_phase8_m2t10 §4.3. First acceptance criterion mandated re-verifying the staleness rejection against current bootstrap logic; second mandated recording the chosen mechanism here.
trigger: Phase-scoped runs (--phase N) bootstrap upstream phases from durable Tier-4 gate results (runner/dag_scheduler.py bootstrap_phase_prerequisites), which calls is_gate_fresh (runner/predicates/gate_pass_predicates.py) to reject stale upstream gates. is_gate_fresh compared the gate result's evaluated_at against the wall-clock mtime of every UPSTREAM_REQUIRED_INPUTS[gate_id] path: if any input's mtime postdated evaluated_at, the gate was STALE. A Tier-3 promote that rewrote docs/tier3_project_instantiation/architecture_inputs/*.json (e.g. adding a provenance field, or a byte-identical re-serialization) bumped their mtimes past the phase 3-6 gate results' evaluated_at, so bootstrap rejected them as stale even when the gate-relevant content was unchanged. mtime is a wall-clock proxy for 'did the input change'; it produces false positives on any rewrite that preserves (or only cosmetically alters) content.
verification: Confirmed live against current code (2026-07-27). is_gate_fresh (gate_pass_predicates.py:137) and its helper _max_upstream_mtime (:74) were purely mtime-based. The gate evaluator (runner/gate_evaluator.py:669) ALREADY records per-artifact SHA-256 fingerprints in the gate result field input_artifact_fingerprints, computed by _compute_fingerprints/_fingerprint_path from the exact same UPSTREAM_REQUIRED_INPUTS[gate_id] list the freshness check reads. So the content evidence needed to judge staleness by content already exists durably in every gate result; ST-1 is the reader side that consumes it. Note: the live phase 1-3 gate_result.json artifacts are separately corrupted by committed git-conflict markers (bffe89d) and their current input content matches neither recorded run's fingerprint — i.e. that live data is genuinely changed, not spuriously stale. ST-1 fixes the mechanism (verified with controlled fixtures); it does NOT and must NOT fabricate freshness for genuinely-changed live artifacts (CLAUDE.md §12.4, §13.7).

decisions.D1_mechanism: Staleness is judged by CONTENT, not wall-clock mtime. is_gate_fresh keeps mtime only as a cheap, conservative TRIGGER: an upstream input whose mtime does not postdate evaluated_at was not touched since evaluation and is definitely unchanged (no hashing needed) -- this preserves today's fast path exactly. When an input's mtime DOES postdate evaluated_at ('mtime-suspect'), freshness is confirmed by CONTENT: the input's current fingerprint (recomputed now) is compared against the fingerprint recorded for that path in the gate result's input_artifact_fingerprints at evaluation time. All mtime-suspect inputs content-match -> FRESH (the mtime bump was spurious). Any suspect's content differs -> STALE. This is a strict RELAXATION of the prior mtime rule: nothing the old code accepted is now rejected; only spurious-mtime false-positives are removed.
decisions.D2_fingerprint_source: The content signal is the input_artifact_fingerprints map the gate evaluator already writes -- not a re-run of the gate and not a Claude re-validation. Freshness stays a pure, deterministic, Claude-free content comparison. This realises exactly the 'recompute input_fingerprint from current inputs' step that CHK-1 decision D4 explicitly deferred to ST-1.
decisions.D3_single_source_of_truth: The fingerprint algorithm is extracted from gate_evaluator.py into a neutral module runner/fingerprints.py (fingerprint_path / compute_fingerprints / MISSING_FINGERPRINT sentinel), imported by BOTH the writer (gate_evaluator) and the reader (gate_pass_predicates.is_gate_fresh). Reader and writer MUST hash identically; divergent algorithms would make content-identical files spuriously mismatch. The bodies are byte-for-byte the former gate_evaluator functions (behaviour-preserving extraction). gate_evaluator now imports compute_fingerprints under its public name (no re-export shim); the only consumers of the old underscore aliases -- tests/runner/test_gate_evaluator.py -- were migrated to import the public names directly from runner.fingerprints. A circular import (gate_evaluator imports gate_pass_recorded from gate_pass_predicates) forbids importing the helper directly from gate_evaluator, which the neutral module also resolves.
decisions.D4_fail_closed: Absent evidence is treated as STALE, never as fresh. If input_artifact_fingerprints is missing entirely (gate results predating the fingerprint field) or a specific mtime-suspect path has no recorded fingerprint to confirm against, that suspect cannot be proven unchanged and is reported stale -- byte-identical to the pre-ST-1 mtime behaviour at that point. The change can only ACCEPT more when positive content evidence proves identity; it never accepts on missing evidence.
decisions.D5_scope: is_gate_fresh is shared by the bootstrap path (dag_scheduler bootstrap_phase_prerequisites) AND the exit-gate path (gate_pass_recorded step 9). The content-based rule applies to BOTH, by design: the same false-positive existed in both, and the invariant 'bootstrap freshness and exit-gate freshness must agree' (tests/runner/test_freshness_scope.py TestBootstrapExitGateConsistency) requires them to stay in lockstep. ST-1 does NOT touch the run_id / continuation-acceptance path (_check_continuation_acceptance, record_accepted_upstream_gate) or the manifest_version staleness axis -- only the upstream-input freshness (step 9) determination.
decisions.D6_directory_input_granularity: For DIRECTORY upstream inputs (e.g. gate_09's lump_sum_budget_planner received/ and validation/ dirs), fingerprint_path hashes only the sorted set of direct-child NAMES (non-recursive), so an in-place change to a child file's BYTES under an unchanged name is not seen and does not make the gate stale. This is a faithful preservation of BOTH the writer's recorded fingerprint semantics AND pre-ST-1 mtime behaviour (a directory's own mtime does not bump on in-place child-content edits), so it is a strict relaxation, not a regression; it is deliberately out of ST-1's Phase-3-6 file-input scope. Recorded so a future reader knows directory-input freshness detects added/removed children, not child-byte edits. Deepening directory fingerprinting to recursive content is a separate, non-ST-1 change.

consistency_with_chk_1: Same bootstrap-evidence contract. CHK-1 (chk-1-checkpoint-provenance-quad_2026-07-24.json) D4 recorded that its checkpoint_published predicate is consistency-only, records the checked input_fingerprint durably, and 'does NOT recompute input_fingerprint from current inputs -- that content-freshness step belongs to ST-1'. ST-1 is that step. The two are complementary and non-overlapping: CHK-1 authorises cross-RUN inheritance (run_id provenance) by set-membership; ST-1 judges input CONTENT freshness by fingerprint. Neither weakens the other; both fail closed on missing/mismatched evidence.
threat_model_boundary: Like CHK-1, this is internal-consistency + false-positive-removal, NOT tamper-proofing against a malicious docs/ writer. Anyone with docs/ write access can rewrite both an input file and the recorded input_artifact_fingerprints; that is out of scope, identical to every other Tier-4 artifact. What ST-1 guarantees: a gate result is judged fresh iff every upstream input's current content matches the content the gate actually evaluated (as recorded at evaluation time), independent of wall-clock mtime.
no_constitutional_amendment_rationale: mtime-vs-content is an implementation detail of the gate_pass_recorded freshness step; the constitution mandates neither. No phase meaning, tier meaning, gate condition, or authority-hierarchy rule changes. §12.4 (missing mandatory inputs trigger gate failure) and §13.7 (no silent weakening of gate conditions) are preserved: genuine content changes and missing evidence still fail closed; only demonstrably-spurious mtime positives are removed. §9.5 (reproducibility) is strengthened -- freshness now derives from content the run can re-derive, not from clock state. Recorded here per §9.4 / §14.1 so a future reader does not mistake this for an un-recorded constitutional change.
change_surface: runner/fingerprints.py (NEW neutral module: fingerprint_path(path), compute_fingerprints(paths, repo_root), MISSING_FINGERPRINT sentinel)
runner/gate_evaluator.py (import compute_fingerprints from runner.fingerprints under its public name; the two fingerprint fn bodies moved out; unused 'import hashlib' dropped)

runner/predicates/gate_pass_predicates.py (is_gate_fresh rewritten: mtime-trigger + content-confirmation via input_artifact_fingerprints; the old mtime-only helper _max_upstream_mtime was REPLACED by _mtime_suspect_inputs, which returns the (path, resolved) suspects instead of a max timestamp)
tests/runner/test_gate_evaluator.py (fingerprint tests migrated to import fingerprint_path/compute_fingerprints from runner.fingerprints; behaviour unchanged)

tests/runner/test_content_staleness.py (NEW: content-identical/newer-mtime accepted; changed-content rejected; fail-closed on missing fingerprints; directory child-set both directions; bootstrap end-to-end both directions)
effect: A phase-scoped run bootstraps an upstream gate whose Tier-3/Tier-4 inputs were rewritten with unchanged content (newer mtime) instead of rejecting it as stale; a genuinely changed input is still rejected. Removes the false-positive that blocked bootstrap after a Tier-3 promote, without weakening genuine-change or missing-evidence detection.
